findings.evidence: Two hard-won traps live only in optional references, not in Gotchas: '<ListItem button>' has no 'button' prop (references/component-recipes.md), and a styled(Button) custom prop named 'variant' collides with Button's own prop (references/sx-and-styled-recipes.md). An agent writing a list or a styled button without loading the recipes will not see them.
findings.fix: Add one Gotchas line for each and keep the full explanation in the reference: '<ListItem button> is not a prop: wrap a ListItemButton in <ListItem disablePadding>' and 'Never name a styled() custom prop after a prop the wrapped component owns (Button variant); filter it with shouldForwardProp'.

findings.evidence: 'Configure Vite for React.', 'Explain CSS specificity.' and 'Explain React server components in Next.js.' are negatives that share nothing with the skill and test nothing. Most positives are terse fragments with no file paths or project context.
findings.fix: Replace the unrelated negatives with near-misses, for example 'Style our Material Web Components (md-filled-button) theme tokens' or 'Fix a CSS specificity fight between Tailwind and our own unlayered CSS'. findings.evidence: Step 3: 'Search the whole repository ... for the legacy APIs ...: `components=`, ... `<Grid item`, ...'. A literal search for '<Grid item' misses multi-line JSX where 'item' sits on the next line after '<Grid', and those legacy props are 'silently ignored' (Gotchas). The migration can therefore miss hits and still pass the typecheck.
findings.fix: Say to search for each prop name on its own (for example a multiline search for '<Grid[^>]*\bitem\b', or the bare 'item' prop inside Grid elements), then confirm with the typecheck. Note that 'components=' also matches non-MUI props, so check each hit's import before migrating it.
